
completion time: 16 hours
improvement points: Connecting with more plot ideas and fast visualizations.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggimage)
library(rsvg) # Required for SVG support
library(showtext) # For custom fonts

result_exact <- read.csv("data/exhibitors_cphijp2026.csv")
# Automatically use showtext for rendering
font_add_google("Sawarabi Gothic", "sawarabi-gothic-regular") # Title font
font_add_google("Noto Sans", "notosans") # Body font
showtext_auto()
```



#  1. Replace flag_url with circular flag URLs (PNG version) 

```{r}
result_exact <- result_exact %>%
  mutate(
    # Replace the flag_url with circular flags from circle-flags
    flag_url = paste0(
      "https://hatscripts.github.io/circle-flags/flags/",
      country_code_lower,
      ".svg"
    )
  ) |>

  mutate(
    region = case_when(
      region == "North America" ~ "North\nAmerica",
      region == "Middle East" ~ "Middle\nEast",
      TRUE ~ region # Keep all other values as they are
    )
  )
# ── 2. Aggregate ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
data <- result_exact %>%
  distinct(
    company_name,
    country,
    country_code_lower,
    flag_url,
    region,
    show_type
  ) |>
  group_by(country, region, flag_url) %>%
  summarise(value = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(region, desc(value))

# ── 3. Add empty bars for spacing ────────────────────────────────────────────
empty_bar <- 3
to_add <- data.frame(matrix(
  NA,
  empty_bar * n_distinct(data$region),
  ncol(data)
))
colnames(to_add) <- colnames(data)
to_add$region <- rep(unique(data$region), each = empty_bar)
data <- rbind(data, to_add)
data <- data %>% arrange(region)
data$id <- seq(1, nrow(data))

# ── 4. Label angles ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
label_data <- data
number_of_bar <- nrow(label_data)
# I substract 0.5 because the letter must have the angle of the center of the bars. Not extreme right(1) or extreme left (0)
angle <- 90 - 360 * (label_data$id - 0.5) / number_of_bar
label_data$hjust <- ifelse(angle < -90, 1, 0)
label_data$angle <- ifelse(angle < -90, angle + 180, angle)

# ── 5. Country flags ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
country_labels <- label_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(country)) %>%
  select(id, country, value, angle, hjust, flag_url)

# ── 6. Region labels ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
region_labels <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(region)) %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(start_id = min(id), end_id = max(id), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    mid_id = (start_id + end_id) / 2,
    angle = 90 - 360 * (mid_id - 0.5) / number_of_bar,
    hjust = 0.5,
    angle = ifelse(angle < -90, angle + 180, angle)
  )

# 6.5 prepare a data frame for base lines
base_data <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(region)) %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarize(start = min(id), end = max(id) - empty_bar) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(title = mean(c(start, end)))

# prepare a data frame for grid (scales)
grid_data <- base_data
grid_data$end <- grid_data$end[c(nrow(grid_data), 1:nrow(grid_data) - 1)] + 1
grid_data$start <- grid_data$start - 1
grid_data <- grid_data[-1, ]

# ── 7. Plot ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
max_value <- max(data$value, na.rm = TRUE)
```


# Visualisation


# Instagram

```{r}

p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = as.factor(id), y = value, fill = region)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", alpha = 0.7, width = 0.9) +

  # Value labels on bars - MUCH LARGER
  geom_text(
    data = label_data %>% filter(!is.na(value)),
    aes(x = id, y = value + max_value * 0.65, label = value, fill = NULL),
    color = "black",
    size = 2, # ← Increased from 5 to 10
    fontface = "bold",
    family = "sawarabi-gothic-regular"
  ) +

  geom_image(
    data = country_labels %>% filter(!is.na(flag_url)),
    aes(x = id, y = value + max_value * 0.25, image = flag_url, fill = NULL),
    size = 0.035, # ← Increased from 0.025 to 0.045
    asp = 1
  ) +

  # Control the circle size
  ylim(-max_value * 2.5, max_value * 1.8) +

  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    # Background color
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#f5f5f5", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#f5f5f5", color = NA),

    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = unit(c(0.2, 0, 0.3, 0), "cm"), # ← CHANGED: reduced top and bottom

    # LARGER Title for Instagram
    plot.title = element_text(
      hjust = 0,
      vjust = -3, # ← CHANGED: negative value moves title DOWN (closer to plot)
      size = 12, # ← Increased from 16 to 32
      face = "bold",
      family = "sawarabi-gothic-regular",
      color = "#2c3e50",
      lineheight = 1.8
    ),

    # LARGER Caption for Instagram
    plot.caption = element_text(
      hjust = 0,
      vjust = 3, # ← CHANGED: positive value moves caption UP (closer to plot)
      size = 5, # ← Increased from 10 to 18
      family = "notosans",
      color = "#7f8c8d",
      lineheight = 1.2
    ),

    text = element_text(family = "notosans")
  ) +

  coord_polar(start = 0) +

  # Title and caption
  labs(
    title = "Chinese Exhibitors Are the Largest \nForeign Presence at CPHI Japan 2026",
    caption = "Source: CPHI Japan 2026 Official Exhibitor List. Date: Jan | 2026"
  ) +

  # Add base line information
  geom_segment(
    data = base_data,
    aes(x = start, y = -10, xend = end, yend = -5),
    colour = "black",
    alpha = 0.5,
    size = 1, # ← Increased from 0.6 to 1.2
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +

  # LARGER Region labels
  geom_text(
    data = base_data,
    aes(x = title, y = -90, label = region),
    hjust = c(1, 0.8, 0, 0),
    colour = "black",
    alpha = 0.8,
    size = 2.2, # ← Increased from 4.5 to 9
    fontface = "bold",
    family = "sawarabi-gothic-regular",
    lineheight = 1.2,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  )

p

```




# Saving

```{r}
library(magick)

# Step 1: Save at Instagram dimensions
ggsave(
  "assets/circular_barplot_temp.png",
  p,
  width = 1080,
  height = 1080,
  units = "px",
  dpi = 150,
  bg = "#f5f5f5"
)

# Step 2: Read plot image
plot_img <- image_read("assets/circular_barplot_temp.png")

# Step 3: Get dimensions
plot_info <- image_info(plot_img)
plot_width <- plot_info$width # 1080
plot_height <- plot_info$height # 1080


# ADD ARROW AND TEXT ANNOTATION

# Step 4: Draw arrow and text on the image
annotated_img <- image_draw(plot_img)

# Define annotation position (RIGHT SIDE)
arrow_start_x <- 850 # Starting point X (near Italy flag)
arrow_start_y <- 550 # Starting point Y (adjust to point at Italy)
arrow_end_x <- 820 # End point X (right side)
arrow_end_y <- 570 # End point Y (where text will be)

text_x <- 850 # Text position X (right side)
text_y <- 520 # Text position Y (above arrow end)

# Draw curved arrow
# Note: base R graphics doesn't have curves, so we'll use a line
# For a curve, we'll draw it as a path
arrows(
  x0 = arrow_start_x,
  y0 = arrow_start_y,
  x1 = arrow_end_x,
  y1 = arrow_end_y,
  col = "#e74c3c", # Red color
  lwd = 3, # Line width
  length = 0.15, # Arrow head size
  angle = 20 # Arrow head angle
)

# Add text annotation
text(
  x = text_x,
  y = text_y,
  labels = "Italy leads European\nexhibitors with 19",
  col = "#2c3e50",
  cex = 2, # Text size
  font = 1, # Bold
  adj = 0 # left:0, center:0.5, right:1
)

# Finish drawing
dev.off()

# ADD LOGO

# Step 5: Add logo
logo_img <- image_read("logos/wide/satom-wide-color.png")
logo_target_width <- round(plot_width * 0.15)
logo_img <- image_scale(logo_img, as.character(logo_target_width))

logo_info <- image_info(logo_img)
logo_width <- logo_info$width
logo_height <- logo_info$height

margin_right <- 30
margin_bottom <- 30

x_offset <- plot_width - logo_width - margin_right
y_offset <- plot_height - logo_height - margin_bottom

# Composite logo onto annotated plot
final_img <- image_composite(
  annotated_img,
  logo_img,
  offset = paste0("+", x_offset, "+", y_offset)
)

# Step 6: Save final image
image_write(
  final_img,
  "assets/circular_barplot_cphijp26_exhibitors_instagram.png",
  quality = 100
)

# Step 7: Display result
print(final_img)
cat("\n✓ Instagram post saved with annotation: 1080x1080px\n")

# Step 8: Clean up
file.remove("assets/circular_barplot_temp.png")
```


# SAVE FOR INSTAGRAM (1080x1080px) WITH LOGO
```{r}

library(magick)
# Step 1: Save at Instagram dimensions
ggsave(
  "assets/circular_barplot_temp.png",
  p,
  width = 1080, # ← Instagram square format
  height = 1080, # ← Instagram square format
  units = "px", # ← Use pixels directly
  dpi = 150, # ← Lower DPI for exact pixel size
  bg = "#f5f5f5"
)

# Step 2: Read both images
plot_img <- image_read("assets/circular_barplot_temp.png")
logo_img <- image_read("logos/wide/satom-wide-color.png")

# Step 3: Get dimensions
plot_info <- image_info(plot_img)
plot_width <- plot_info$width # Should be 1080
plot_height <- plot_info$height # Should be 1080

# Step 4: Resize logo for Instagram (15% of width)
logo_target_width <- round(plot_width * 0.15) # About 160px
logo_img <- image_scale(logo_img, as.character(logo_target_width))

logo_info <- image_info(logo_img)
logo_width <- logo_info$width
logo_height <- logo_info$height

# Step 5: Position at BOTTOM-RIGHT corner
margin_right <- 30 # pixels from right edge
margin_bottom <- 30 # pixels from bottom edge

x_offset <- plot_width - logo_width - margin_right
y_offset <- plot_height - logo_height - margin_bottom

# Step 6: Composite logo onto plot
final_img <- image_composite(
  plot_img,
  logo_img,
  offset = paste0("+", x_offset, "+", y_offset)
)

# Step 7: Save final Instagram-ready image
image_write(
  final_img,
  "assets/circular_barplot_cphijp26_exhibitors_instagram.png",
  quality = 100
)

# Step 8: Display the final result
print(final_img)

# Step 9: Clean up temporary file
file.remove("assets/circular_barplot_temp.png")
```
